title: Tech news today, 27 November 2026

items.headline: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
items.summary: The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks […]
lines: Reported by The Verge: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year.
The article says the watch has a smaller-wrist fit, an OLED touchscreen, and good battery life, and it describes the reviewer's testing.
The item is a consumer deal and does not address business or IT use.

items.headline: Backloggd urges users to change their passwords after a breach
items.summary: If you use Backloggd, you might need to log in again and reset your password.
lines: Reported by Engadget: Backloggd urges users to change their passwords after a breach.
Users may need to log in again and reset their password.
Staff who use the service may need to reset their credentials, and IT teams may want to confirm whether any work accounts share those logins.

items.headline: Fake paid expert interviews impersonate brands to steal Google logins
items.summary: An ongoing phishing campaign dubbed "GoodGuys" impersonates major brands, including Google, Nvidia, Accenture, and SpaceX, to steal corporate Google and Okta credentials using fake invitations to paid expert interviews and webinars. [...]
lines: Reported by BleepingComputer: An ongoing phishing campaign called "GoodGuys" impersonates brands including Google, Nvidia, Accenture, and SpaceX to steal corporate Google and Okta credentials.
The campaign uses fake invitations to paid expert interviews and webinars.
IT teams may want to warn staff to be cautious with unsolicited interview or webinar invitations that ask them to sign in.

items.headline: ThreatsDay: 10M NGINX Services at Risk, 250+ Malicious Extensions, AI Server Hijacking + 17 More Stories
items.summary: A website can look perfectly fine to the person running it. Log out, visit the same page, and things might look different. Something similar is happening with browser extensions, where even the way you find and install one can change what it does. Checking whether software works as expected only tells you so much. Then there’s the question of who gets to use what. Stolen logins are opening
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: The ThreatsDay roundup lists 10M NGINX services at risk, 250+ malicious browser extensions, and AI server hijacking.
Admins who run NGINX or manage browser extensions may want to review their exposure to these items.

items.headline: VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.2 の一般提供（GA）を開始
items.summary: 多くの企業がスピードの向上、コストの削減、セキュリティの強化を目指す一方で、新たな収益源を生み出すためにアプリケーションやワークロードの幅を広げ続けるプレッシャーにも直面しています。VMware Cloud Foundation（VCF）9.1.2 の一般提供（GA）は、こうした課題に直接応えるものであり、新たな AI 自動化機能に加え、VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service（VKS）の機能強化やセキュリティアップデートを提供します。これらのアップデートにより、プラットフォームチームは手動での構成作業にかける時間を減らし、ビジネス価値の創出により多くの時間を割けるようになります。 本記事では、VCF 9.1.2 で追加された主な新機能について詳しくご紹介します。 AI インフラストラクチャのデプロイを自動化 これまで AI ワークロード用のインフラストラクチャを構築するには、複数の手動ステップをつなぎ合わせる必要がありました。VCF 9.1.2 では、単一の VMware vCenter プラグインを通じて Day 0 のデプロイを自動化する「AI インフラストラクチャ・クイックスタート」を導入し、クラスター構成、VMware vSphere Supervisor の有効化、VKS クラスターのセットアップを 1 つの合理化されたワークフローに統合しました。 これにより、チームは基盤となるインフラストラクチャとソフトウェアを 1 つの連携したステップでプロビジョニングできるようになります。長期にわたる手動設定に悩まされることなく、デプロイまでの時間を
lines: VMware by Broadcom launched general availability (GA) of VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) 9.1.2, with new AI automation features, enhancements to VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS), and security updates.

The AI Infrastructure Quickstart uses a single VMware vCenter plugin to automate Day 0 deployment, combining cluster configuration, enabling VMware vSphere Supervisor, and VKS cluster setup into one workflow.
Platform teams can spend less time on manual configuration and more time on business value, and provision infrastructure and software in one coordinated sequence of steps.

items.headline: Instagram for TV Comes to India, Introducing New Ways to Watch Reels Together
items.summary: Instagram for TV will soon be available in India, bringing content from your favorite creators to the big screen in your home so you can enjoy watching them with friends. The post Instagram for TV Comes to India, Introducing New Ways to Watch Reels Together appeared first on Meta Newsroom .
lines: Instagram for TV will soon be available in India, bringing Reels from favorite creators to the big screen at home.
It also adds new ways to watch Reels together with friends.

items.headline: Mastering CBAM Compliance: What SAP’s Latest Release Means for Declarants
items.summary: Businesses have less than a year to ensure their often manual and fragmented compliance processes are ready.
lines: SAP's latest release is aimed at helping declarants meet CBAM compliance requirements.
Businesses have less than a year to make their often manual and fragmented compliance processes ready.
Teams responsible for CBAM compliance may need to review those manual processes.

items.headline: New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges
items.summary: ​A 12-year-old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Network File System (NFS) server, tracked as CVE-2026-99362, allows remote attackers to gain root privileges. [...]
lines: Reported by BleepingComputer: A 12-year-old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel's NFS server, tracked as CVE-2026-99362, allows remote attackers to gain root privileges.
The flaw is called NFS2ROOT.
IT teams running Linux systems with NFS servers should review their exposure to this flaw.

items.headline: WhatsApp security alert: Govt flags 5 ‘high risk’ flaws, one may have been exploited
items.summary: According to CERT-In, attackers can use flaws by sending a message, file or link. Code on user device can be used to get hold of info, or bypass app's security checks.
lines: Reported by ThePrint: Tech: CERT-In flagged 5 'high risk' WhatsApp flaws, and one may have been exploited.
According to CERT-In, attackers can use the flaws by sending a message, file or link.
Code on a user device can be used to get hold of information or bypass the app's security checks.
IT teams may need to assess WhatsApp use on managed devices.

items.headline: Jio launches and takes down astrology platform within a day
items.summary: Amidst AstroTalk becoming unavailable on Apple's app store, Jio launched an AI-powered astrology platform on Nov 26 and took it down after a few hours, saying that the live website was just a "demo survey". The post Jio launches and takes down astrology platform within a day appeared first on MEDIANAMA .
lines: Reported by MediaNama: Jio launched an AI-powered astrology platform on Nov 26 and took it down after a few hours.
Jio said the live website was just a 'demo survey'.
The launch came amid AstroTalk becoming unavailable on Apple's app store.

items.headline: Hackers Trojanize Official Q-Dir and DesktopOK Downloads to Deliver Remote Access Malware
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a software supply chain attack that has tampered with Q-Dir and DesktopOK installation files distributed via the official SoftwareOK website. "Evidence indicates that malicious files were generated not only when users downloaded the programs directly from the official download page but also during the update process of previously installed
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Attackers trojanized Q-Dir and DesktopOK installation files distributed via the official SoftwareOK website.
Researchers say malicious files were generated on direct downloads from the official download page and during updates of previously installed programs.
The tampered files were used to deliver remote access malware.
IT teams that deploy these tools should verify installation files and update sources.

items.headline: Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators
items.summary: Attackers using AI agents have broken into computer systems at Swiss organizations in four of five confirmed attacks, the first such cases in the country, the country's cybersecurity agency said yesterday. Three of the attacks targeted critical infrastructure operators, and two of those succeeded, with no major disruptions reported. The victims have not been named, and it is not known who is
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Switzerland's cybersecurity agency confirmed that attackers using AI agents broke into systems at Swiss organizations in four of five confirmed attacks.
Three attacks targeted critical infrastructure operators, and two of those succeeded, with no major disruptions reported.
These are the first such cases in the country.

items.headline: Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access
items.summary: Details have emerged about a new zero-day vulnerability in Cacti, an open-source network monitoring tool, that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution. The proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, which has yet to be assigned a CVE identifier, has been tracked as 4HTTP2SHELL and 4HTTP2ROOT. "I found a path from a fresh, unauthenticated HTTP session to command execution as the Cacti server
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Details have emerged about an unpatched zero-day in Cacti, an open-source network monitoring tool, that could enable remote code execution.
The proof-of-concept exploit has been tracked as 4HTTP2SHELL and 4HTTP2ROOT and has not yet been assigned a CVE identifier.
The exploit reportedly needs only four HTTP requests via guest access.
IT teams running Cacti should review guest access settings and exposure.
